points.title: 早年成长
points.description: 亚里士多德出生于希腊北部的斯塔吉拉，其父亲尼各马可是马其顿国王阿敏塔斯三世的御医。这一优越的家庭背景使亚里士多德从小接受了良好的教育。在斯塔吉拉的童年时期，他不仅学习了基本的希腊文化知识，还可能接触到了医学知识，这对他后来注重观察和分类的科学方法产生了深远影响。公元前367年，父亲去世后，亚里士多德被监护人普洛克森努斯送往雅典。
points.descriptionEn: Aristotle was born in Stagira, a city in northern Greece. His father, Nicomachus, was the personal physician to King Amyntas III of Macedon. This privileged background provided Aristotle with an excellent education. During his childhood in Stagira, not only did he learn basic Greek culture, but he may also have been exposed to medical knowledge, which profoundly influenced his later scientific methods of observation and classification. After his father's death in 367 BC, Aristotle was sent to Athens under the care of his guardian Proxenus.

points.title: 柏拉图学院
points.description: 抵达雅典后，亚里士多德进入柏拉图学园学习，师从柏拉图长达20年。在这段时期，他深入研究了哲学、数学、科学等多个领域，逐渐形成了自己的思想体系。亚里士多德与柏拉图在理念论上存在分歧，他更注重经验观察而非抽象理念。柏拉图去世后，亚里士多德离开雅典，前往小亚细亚的阿索斯游学，并娶了皮西阿斯的女儿皮西阿斯为妻。雅典时期是亚里士多德思想形成的关键阶段，为他后来的学术成就奠定了坚实基础。
points.descriptionEn: After arriving in Athens, Aristotle entered Plato's Academy, where he studied for twenty years under the great philosopher. During this period, he delved into philosophy, mathematics, science, and other fields, gradually forming his own philosophical system. Aristotle differed from Plato on the theory of Forms, emphasizing empirical observation over abstract ideals. After Plato's death, Aristotle left Athens and traveled to Assos in Asia Minor, where he married Pythias, the daughter of his friend Pythias. His time in Athens was crucial for the development of his thought and laid the foundation for his later achievements.

points.title: 科学研究
points.description: 离开雅典后，亚里士多德前往小亚细亚的阿索斯，在那里建立了自己的学园，并开始进行系统的科学研究。他与好友泰奥弗拉斯托斯一起研究生物学，特别是海洋生物学。随后，他移居到莱斯博斯岛的米蒂利尼，继续进行生物学研究。这一时期，亚里士多德对超过500种动物进行了分类研究，撰写了《动物志》等著作。他通过解剖和观察，提出了许多关于生物学、胚胎学和生态学的开创性理论，这些研究使他成为古代最伟大的生物学家之一。
points.descriptionEn: After leaving Athens, Aristotle traveled to Assos in Asia Minor, where he established his own school and began systematic scientific research. Together with his friend Theophrastus, he studied biology, particularly marine biology. Later, he moved to Mytilene on the island of Lesbos, continuing his biological research. During this period, Aristotle classified over 500 species of animals and wrote works such as 'History of Animals.' Through dissection and observation, he developed pioneering theories in biology, embryology, and ecology, establishing himself as one of the greatest ancient biologists.

points.title: 马其顿宫廷
points.description: 公元前343年，亚里士多德应马其顿国王腓力二世的邀请，前往首都佩拉，担任年仅13岁的亚历山大大帝的私人教师。在马其顿宫廷的三年间，亚里士多德不仅教授亚历山大哲学、伦理学、政治学和科学知识，还向他灌输了希腊文化的优越性。这段经历对亚历山大的思想产生了深远影响，也使亚里士多德得以接触马其顿的政治和军事体系。这段教学经历使亚里士多德能够将理论与实践相结合，为他后来的政治哲学研究提供了宝贵素材。
points.descriptionEn: In 343 BC, Aristotle was invited by King Philip II of Macedon to Pella, the capital, to become the private tutor to the 13-year-old Alexander the Great. During his three years at the Macedonian court, Aristotle taught Alexander philosophy, ethics, politics, and science, instilling in him the superiority of Greek culture. This experience profoundly influenced Alexander's thinking and allowed Aristotle to observe the Macedonian political and military systems firsthand. This teaching experience enabled Aristotle to combine theory with practice, providing valuable material for his later political philosophy.

points.title: 吕克昂学园
points.description: 公元前335年，亚里士多德重返雅典，在城外的吕克昂体育场创办了自己的学园。与柏拉图的学园不同，亚里士多德的学园更注重实证研究和科学探索，学生们在林荫道上边散步边讨论，因此被称为'逍遥学派'。在吕克昂期间，亚里士多德完成了大量著作，涵盖逻辑学、物理学、形而上学、伦理学、政治学、生物学等多个领域。他建立了系统的分类体系，创立了形式逻辑，对后世科学发展产生了深远影响。公元前323年亚历山大大帝去世后，雅典反马其顿情绪高涨，亚里士多德被迫离开雅典，次年去世于优卑亚岛的卡尔基斯。
points.descriptionEn: In 335 BC, Aristotle returned to Athens and founded his own school, the Lyceum, located outside the city walls in a gymnasium. Unlike Plato's Academy, the Lyceum emphasized empirical research and scientific inquiry. Students would discuss while walking along the shaded paths, earning the school the name 'Peripatetic' (meaning 'to walk around'). During his time at the Lyceum, Aristotle produced numerous works covering logic, physics, metaphysics, ethics, politics, biology, and other fields. He established systematic classification systems and formal logic, profoundly influencing the development of science. After Alexander the Great's death in 323 BC, anti-Macedonian sentiment in Athens grew, forcing Aristotle to leave the city. He died the following year in Chalcis, Euboea.

appraisal.zh: 亚里士多德被誉为百科全书式的学者，其思想体系几乎涵盖全部知识领域，逻辑学方法为科学发展提供基础，伦理学与政治学深刻影响西方政治传统，生物学研究开创科学分类先河，其遗产塑造西方文明两千余年。也有研究者指出，他为奴隶制与女性从属地位辩护，自然解释带有目的论色彩，诸多科学结论后被证伪，如重物下落更快的说法，其体系被认为过于保守。总体而言，他既是古代知识体系的集大成者，也是不断被重新诠释与批判的关键转折点。
appraisal.en: Aristotle is hailed as an encyclopedic scholar whose system spans nearly every field of knowledge, whose logic provided a foundation for science, whose ethics and politics shaped the Western tradition, and whose biology pioneered classification, his legacy molding Western civilization for over two millennia. Yet researchers also note his defenses of slavery and women's subordination, the teleological cast of his natural explanations, and scientific conclusions later disproven, such as heavier objects falling faster; some deem his system too conservative. Overall he is both the culmination of ancient knowledge and a pivotal point continually reinterpreted and criticized.

supporter.zh: 亚里士多德被誉为'百科全书式的学者'，他的思想体系几乎涵盖了人类知识的所有领域。支持者认为他是西方哲学的奠基人之一，其逻辑学方法为科学发展提供了基础。他的伦理学和政治学理论深刻影响了西方政治传统，而他的生物学研究则开创了科学分类的先河。亚里士多德强调理性与观察相结合的方法，为后世科学研究树立了典范，其思想遗产持续影响了西方文明两千多年。
supporter.en: Aristotle is hailed as an 'encyclopedic scholar' whose philosophical system encompasses nearly all fields of human knowledge. Supporters consider him one of the founders of Western philosophy, with his logical methods providing the foundation for scientific development. His ethical and political theories profoundly influenced Western political tradition, while his biological research pioneered scientific classification. Aristotle's emphasis on combining reason with observation established a model for scientific inquiry, and his intellectual legacy has shaped Western civilization for over two millennia.

critic.zh: 批评者指出亚里士多德的体系存在诸多局限，包括对奴隶制和女性地位的辩护，以及他对自然现象的解释常带有目的论色彩。他的许多科学结论后来被证明是错误的，如认为重物下落速度与其重量成正比。此外，亚里士多德对柏拉图理念论的批判虽然推动了哲学发展，但也导致了对抽象思维的轻视。一些现代学者认为他的思想体系过于保守，阻碍了科学革命前的思想创新。
critic.en: Critics point out numerous limitations in Aristotle's system, including his justifications for slavery and the subordinate status of women, as well as his teleological explanations of natural phenomena. Many of his scientific conclusions were later proven incorrect, such as his belief that heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones. Additionally, while Aristotle's critique of Plato's theory of Forms advanced philosophy, it also led to a devaluation of abstract thinking. Some modern scholars argue that his system was too conservative, hindering intellectual innovation before the scientific revolution.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，亚里士多德被视为古代知识体系的集大成者，他的著作保存了古希腊文明的许多重要思想。在流行文化中，他常被描绘为智慧与理性的象征，影响着从文艺复兴到现代科学的发展轨迹。亚里士多德的思想既被尊为经典，也不断被重新诠释和批判，体现了人类知识演变的辩证过程。他的方法论贡献与具体理论错误同样重要，共同构成了西方思想史上的关键转折点。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Aristotle is regarded as the culmination of ancient knowledge systems, whose works preserved many important ideas of Greek civilization. In popular culture, he is often depicted as a symbol of wisdom and reason, influencing intellectual development from the Renaissance to modern science. Aristotle's thought is both revered as a classic and constantly reinterpreted and criticized, reflecting the dialectical process of intellectual evolution. Both his methodological contributions and specific theoretical errors are equally important, constituting a pivotal point in the history of Western thought.

self.en: I love Plato, but I love truth more.
